summary: Dagfinn Føllesdal was a philosopher who studied at the University of Oslo (~1950–1957) and Harvard University (~1957–1961) under Willard Van Orman Quine. He held major academic posts at the University of Oslo (~1967–1999) and Stanford University (~1968–2026).
Dagmar Schwerk is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her doctoral studies at the University of Hamburg (~2012–2017) under the supervision of Dorji Wangchuk.
Daijo Tokiwa was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1896–1899), he held a post at Toyo University from approximately 1904 to 1939.

Daiju Sasaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (~1996–2007). In 2015, he held posts as a part-time lecturer at Taisho University and as a full-time lecturer at Chisan Denpoin.

Dainin Katagiri was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under traditional teacher Eko Hashimoto (~1946–1953) and at Komazawa University (~1948–1951). He later founded the Minnesota Zen Meditation Center.

Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Waseda and Tokyo universities. He held key posts at Tokyo Imperial University, Otani University, Columbia University, Matsugaoka Bunko, and Sekai Seiten Kanko Kyokai.

Daishun Ueyama was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Akira Fujieda (~1960–1970). He held posts at Ryukoku University, serving as assistant professor (~1970–1980) and later as president in 1983.

Dale S. Wright is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under Alan Anderson, Wang Pachow, and Robert Scharlemann, and served as a professor of religious and Asian studies at Occidental College (~1980–2019).

Dalsukh D. Malvania was an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar. He held an attested post at Banaras Hindu University in 1951 and served as Director of the L.D. Institute of Indology, attested from 1965 to 1971.
Damdin Badaraev is a scholar in Tibetology and linguistics who studied under Bidya Dandaron and George Roerich.

Damien Keown is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy who earned degrees at Lancaster University and the University of Oxford. He held a post at Goldsmiths, University of London (~1990–2013), and founded the Journal of Buddhist Ethics.

Damodar Dharmananda Kosambi was an Indologist and historian who studied at Harvard University (~1926–1929) and Fergusson College (~1932–1946). He held an academic post at Banaras Hindu University from approximately 1930 to 1931.

Dan Arnold is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology who studied at Carleton College and the University of Chicago. He has held positions at McGill University, the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, and the University of Chicago (~2003).

Dan Lusthaus is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed his Ph.D. at Temple University. He has taught at Grinnell College, Bates College, Macalester College, Florida State University, the University of Georgia, and Harvard University.

Dan Martin is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed his Ph.D. at Indiana University (~1984–1991). He held positions at the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters, the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, and Carnegie Mellon University.

Dan Smyer Yü is a scholar in religious studies and Tibetology who completed his PhD at the University of California, Davis. He served as a Research Group Leader at the Max Planck Institute for the Study of Religious and Ethnic Diversity.

Dan Zahavi is a philosopher who completed a PhD at KU Leuven (~1989–1994) and a Habilitation at the University of Copenhagen (~1995–1999). Around 2002, he became Professor and Director of the Center for Subjectivity Research at Copenhagen.

Daniel A. Getz is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at Yale University under Stanley Weinstein, attested in 1994, and later held a post as associate professor at Bradley University, attested in 2019.

Daniel Aitken is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Tasmania under the supervision of Jay L. Garfield, and also studied under Parimal G. Patil and Leonard van der Kuijp.
Daniel Amadé Scheidegger is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and religious studies. He completed his doctoral degree at the University of Bristol under the supervision of Paul Williams.
